files.doc:
Pass 1: facts about ONE Python file (ADR-0003).

Pure function of (path, source): it never reads other files, so its result can be cached by
content hash. Everything that needs other files (resolving names, types, calls) is pass 2.

Facts are plain JSON-serialisable dicts:
  imports    [{alias, target, line}]              alias bound in this module -> dotted target
  classes    [{name, line, end_line, bases, decorators, doc, attr_types}]
  functions  [{qualname, name, cls, line, end_line, params, returns, is_async, decorators,
               doc, calls, vars, sql}]          (+ one "<module>" pseudo-function for top-level code)
  module_vars {name: type_spec}                    type_spec = {"ann": str} | {"call": chain}
  routes     [{verb, path, function, receiver, line}]
A call "chain" is the callee written as tokens: `a.b().c` -> ["a", "b", "()", "c"].
Map a repository: find Python files, run pass 1 (cached) and pass 2, assemble the world.

"""Map a repository: find Python files, run pass 1 (cached) and pass 2, assemble the world."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import subprocess
import time
from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
from concurrent.futures.process import BrokenProcessPool
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path

from projectviewer import __version__
from projectviewer.cache import Cache

from .extract import EXTRACTOR_VERSION, extract
from .resolve import build_world

SKIP_DIRS = {"node_modules", "venv", "env", "__pycache__", "site-packages", "build", "dist"}
# Below this many cache misses, starting worker processes costs more than it saves (measured: see
# docs/project-status.md). Typical incremental updates touch a handful of files and stay serial.
PARALLEL_MIN_FILES = 64


def _git(root: Path, *args: str) -> str | None:
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(root), *args], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
        return r.stdout
    except (FileNotFoundError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
        return None


def _keep(rel: str) -> bool:
    parts = rel.split("/")
    return rel.endswith(".py") and not any(p.startswith(".") or p in SKIP_DIRS for p in parts[:-1])


def discover(root: Path) -> list[str]:
    """Python files, as repo-relative posix paths. Uses git (respects .gitignore, includes new
    untracked files) when available, otherwise walks the directory."""
    listed = _git(root, "ls-files", "--cached", "--others", "--exclude-standard", "-z")
    if listed is not None:
        paths = [p for p in listed.split("\0") if p]
    else:
        paths = [p.relative_to(root).as_posix() for p in root.rglob("*.py")]
    return sorted(p for p in set(paths) if _keep(p) and (root / p).is_file())


def _extract_job(job: tuple[str, bytes]) -> dict:
    rel, data = job
    return extract(rel, data.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"))


def git_files(root: Path, rev: str) -> list[tuple[str, bytes]]:
    """(path, content) of the Python files in a commit, read from git objects: the working tree is
    never touched. One `git cat-file --batch` process for all files."""
    listed = _git(root, "ls-tree", "-r", "-z", "--name-only", rev)
    if listed is None:
        return []
    paths = sorted(p for p in listed.split("\0") if p and _keep(p))
    if not paths:
        return []
    proc = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", str(root), "cat-file", "--batch"],
        input="".join(f"{rev}:{p}\n" for p in paths).encode(),
        capture_output=True,
        check=True,
    )
    out, pos, items = proc.stdout, 0, []
    for p in paths:
        nl = out.index(b"\n", pos)
        header = out[pos:nl].split()
        pos = nl + 1
        if len(header) < 3 or header[1] != b"blob":  # "missing" or not a file
            continue
        size = int(header[2])
        items.append((p, out[pos : pos + size]))
        pos += size + 1  # content is followed by a newline
    return items


def _analyse(
    items: list[tuple[str, bytes]], cache: Cache | None, workers: int | None
) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
    """Pass 1 for (path, bytes) items: from the cache when possible, parsed (maybe in parallel) otherwise."""
    files: list[dict | None] = [None] * len(items)
    todo: list[tuple[int, str, bytes, str | None]] = []  # (index, path, bytes, cache key)
    for i, (rel, data) in enumerate(items):
        key = Cache.key(EXTRACTOR_VERSION, rel, data) if cache else None
        facts = cache.get(key) if cache else None
        if facts is None:
            todo.append((i, rel, data, key))
        else:
            files[i] = facts

    n_workers = workers or (min(os.cpu_count() or 1, 8) if len(todo) >= PARALLEL_MIN_FILES else 1)
    jobs = [(rel, data) for _, rel, data, _ in todo]
    results = None
    if n_workers > 1:
        try:
            with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=n_workers) as pool:  # pass 1 is pure: safe to parallelise
                results = list(pool.map(_extract_job, jobs, chunksize=16))
        except (BrokenProcessPool, OSError):
            # e.g. called from a REPL/stdin on macOS, where "spawn" workers cannot re-import __main__
            results = None
    if results is None:
        results = [_extract_job(j) for j in jobs]
    for (i, _, _, key), facts in zip(todo, results, strict=True):
        files[i] = facts
        if cache:
            cache.put(key, facts)
    return files, len(todo)


def _world(root: Path, items, cache, workers, commit, dirty) -> dict:
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    files, misses = _analyse(items, cache, workers)
    t1 = time.perf_counter()
    nodes, edges, stats = build_world(files)
    t2 = time.perf_counter()
    stats.update(
        files={"total": len(files), "errors": sum(1 for f in files if f["error"])},
        cache={"enabled": cache is not None, "hits": len(files) - misses, "misses": misses},
        seconds={"extract": round(t1 - t0, 4), "resolve": round(t2 - t1, 4), "total": round(t2 - t0, 4)},
    )
    return {
        "schema": "project-world/1",
        "generated_by": f"projectviewer {__version__} (python analyser v{EXTRACTOR_VERSION})",
        "repo": str(root),
        "commit": commit,
        "dirty": dirty,
        "generated_at": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        "nodes": nodes,
        "edges": edges,
        "stats": stats,
    }


def map_repo(root: Path, cache: Cache | None = None, workers: int | None = None) -> dict:
    """The working tree (including uncommitted and untracked files). workers: processes for parsing
    cache misses. None = automatic (parallel only when there are enough misses); 1 = always serial."""
    root = Path(root).resolve()
    items = [(rel, (root / rel).read_bytes()) for rel in discover(root)]
    head = _git(root, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
    status = _git(root, "status", "--porcelain")
    dirty = bool(status.strip()) if status is not None else None
    return _world(root, items, cache, workers, head.strip() if head else None, dirty)


def map_revision(root: Path, rev: str, cache: Cache | None = None, workers: int | None = None) -> dict:
    """A commit, read from git objects (the working tree is not touched)."""
    root = Path(root).resolve()
    sha = _git(root, "rev-parse", rev)
    return _world(root, git_files(root, rev), cache, workers, sha.strip() if sha else None, False)

files.doc:
Pass 2: link per-file facts into one world: nodes + edges (ADR-0002).

No parsing happens here, only lookups in memory, so it is fast even when every file came from
the cache. Resolution is deliberately conservative: a call is linked only when the target can be
derived from definitions, imports, `self`, or simple type information. Everything else is
*counted* (external / builtin / unresolved), never guessed.

Content-addressed cache of per-file analysis results (ADR-0003).

Key = sha256(analyser version, file path, file bytes). Unchanged files are never parsed twice,
across commits, branches and repositories. Lives outside analysed projects (~/.cache/projectviewer).

What changed, where, why, and what it affects.

A change set compares two worlds: a commit with its parent, or the live working copy with HEAD.
- changed:    nodes whose lines changed ("modified"), that did not exist before ("new"), or that only
              contain changed members ("contains")
- removed:    nodes that no longer exist
- upstream:   who depends on the change (callers, endpoints, tests): {node: steps away}
- downstream: what the change reaches (callees, tables): {node: steps away}
- notes:      the author's explanation per symbol, from the commit message's "Changes:" section
              (`- path::Qualified.name: text` or `- path: text`). Ported and adapted from PR World
              v5's world_diff (same idea: line ranges of the diff, then impact through the graph).

"""projectviewer command line."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from projectviewer.analyzers.python import map_repo
from projectviewer.cache import Cache


def _summary(world: dict) -> str:
    s = world["stats"]
    n, c = s["nodes"], s["calls"]
    linked = c["resolved"] / max(1, c["resolved"] + c["unresolved_named"])
    return (
        f"{s['files']['total']} files ({s['files']['errors']} with errors) · "
        f"{n.get('class', 0)} classes · {n.get('function', 0)} functions · "
        f"{n.get('endpoint', 0)} endpoints · {n.get('table', 0)} tables · {sum(s['edges'].values())} links\n"
        f"calls: {c['resolved']} linked, {c['unresolved']} unresolved, of which {c['unresolved_named']} "
        f"look like project calls ({linked:.0%} linked) · {c['external']} to libraries, {c['builtin']} builtin, "
        f"{c['local']} to inner functions · HTTP: {s['http']['matched']}/{s['http']['total']} test requests "
        f"matched to endpoints\n"
        f"cache: {s['cache']['hits']} hits / {s['cache']['misses']} misses · "
        f"{s['seconds']['total'] * 1000:.0f} ms (extract {s['seconds']['extract'] * 1000:.0f}, "
        f"resolve {s['seconds']['resolve'] * 1000:.0f})"
    )


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv
    if argv[:1] == ["hook"]:  # Claude Code hook: fast path, never fails (see hook.py)
        from projectviewer.hook import main as hook_main

        return hook_main(argv[1:])
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="projectviewer", description=__doc__)
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    m = sub.add_parser("map", help="Map a repository into a project-world/1 JSON document")
    m.add_argument("root", type=Path, help="repository to map")
    m.add_argument("-o", "--output", type=Path, help="write the world here (default: stdout)")
    m.add_argument("--no-cache", action="store_true", help="analyse every file again")
    m.add_argument("--cache-dir", type=Path, help="cache location (default: ~/.cache/projectviewer)")
    s = sub.add_parser("serve", help="Open the live viewer for your subscribed projects (and any given here)")
    s.add_argument("roots", type=Path, nargs="*", help="repositories to add before serving")
    s.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8765)
    s.add_argument("--open", action="store_true", help="open the browser")
    s.add_argument("--cache-dir", type=Path, help="cache location (default: ~/.cache/projectviewer)")
    a = sub.add_parser("add", help="Subscribe a repository (shown in the viewer)")
    a.add_argument("root", type=Path)
    r = sub.add_parser("remove", help="Unsubscribe a repository (by id or path)")
    r.add_argument("project")
    sub.add_parser("list", help="List subscribed repositories")
    sub.add_parser(
        "hook", help="Claude Code hook: report AI activity to the viewer (reads the event on stdin)"
    )
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    if args.cmd in ("add", "remove", "list"):
        from projectviewer import registry

        if args.cmd == "add":
            if not args.root.is_dir():
                ap.error(f"not a directory: {args.root}")
            p = registry.add(args.root)
            print(f"subscribed: {p['id']}  {p['path']}")
        elif args.cmd == "remove":
            print("removed" if registry.remove(args.project) else f"not subscribed: {args.project}")
        for p in registry.load() if args.cmd == "list" else []:
            print(f"{p['id']:24s} {p['path']}")
        return 0

    if args.cmd == "serve":
        from projectviewer import registry
        from projectviewer.server import make_server

        for root in args.roots:
            if not root.is_dir():
                ap.error(f"not a directory: {root}")
            registry.add(root)
        subscribed = registry.load()
        if not subscribed:
            ap.error("no projects yet: run `projectviewer add <repo>` or `projectviewer serve <repo>`")
        srv = make_server(
            [Path(p["path"]) for p in subscribed],
            port=args.port,
            cache=Cache(args.cache_dir),
            ids=[p["id"] for p in subscribed],
        )
        url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{srv.server_address[1]}"
        names = ", ".join(p["id"] for p in subscribed)
        print(f"projectViewer: {names} -> {url}   (Ctrl+C to stop)", file=sys.stderr)
        if args.open:
            import webbrowser

            webbrowser.open(url)
        try:
            srv.serve_forever()
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            pass
        finally:
            srv.server_close()
        return 0

    if args.cmd == "map":
        if not args.root.is_dir():
            ap.error(f"not a directory: {args.root}")
        world = map_repo(args.root, cache=None if args.no_cache else Cache(args.cache_dir))
        text = json.dumps(world, separators=(",", ":"))
        if args.output:
            args.output.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        else:
            sys.stdout.write(text + "\n")
        print(_summary(world), file=sys.stderr)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

`projectviewer hook`: a Claude Code hook that tells the local viewer what the AI is doing.

Configured in Claude Code settings for PostToolUse (Edit|Write|MultiEdit), UserPromptSubmit and Stop.
Claude Code passes the event as JSON on stdin (fields per the Claude Code hooks reference:
hook_event_name, session_id, cwd, tool_name, tool_input.file_path, prompt).

Rules (ADR-0001): it must never slow down or break the developer. It sends one small local request
with a short timeout, ignores every error, prints nothing and always exits 0, so Claude Code sees
"no decision" and carries on, whether or not the viewer is running. Prompt text is sent only with
--prompts, and stays on this machine.

"""`projectviewer hook`: a Claude Code hook that tells the local viewer what the AI is doing.

Configured in Claude Code settings for PostToolUse (Edit|Write|MultiEdit), UserPromptSubmit and Stop.
Claude Code passes the event as JSON on stdin (fields per the Claude Code hooks reference:
hook_event_name, session_id, cwd, tool_name, tool_input.file_path, prompt).

Rules (ADR-0001): it must never slow down or break the developer. It sends one small local request
with a short timeout, ignores every error, prints nothing and always exits 0, so Claude Code sees
"no decision" and carries on, whether or not the viewer is running. Prompt text is sent only with
--prompts, and stays on this machine.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
import urllib.request

DEFAULT_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/events"
MAX_PROMPT = 500


def event_from_hook(raw: dict, prompts: bool) -> dict:
    ev = {
        "event": raw.get("hook_event_name"),
        "session": raw.get("session_id"),
        "cwd": raw.get("cwd"),
    }
    if raw.get("tool_name"):
        ev["tool"] = raw["tool_name"]
    file_path = (raw.get("tool_input") or {}).get("file_path")
    if file_path:
        ev["file"] = file_path
    if prompts and raw.get("prompt"):
        ev["prompt"] = raw["prompt"][:MAX_PROMPT]
    return {k: v for k, v in ev.items() if v is not None}


def send(event: dict, url: str = DEFAULT_URL, timeout: float = 0.3) -> None:
    try:
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=json.dumps(event).encode(), method="POST")
        req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        req.add_header("X-ProjectViewer", "1")
        urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout).close()
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - the viewer may be closed; never disturb the developer
        pass


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    try:
        ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="projectviewer hook")
        ap.add_argument("--prompts", action="store_true", help="also send the prompt text (local only)")
        ap.add_argument("--url", default=DEFAULT_URL)
        args = ap.parse_args(argv)
        raw = json.loads(sys.stdin.read() or "{}")
        if isinstance(raw, dict):
            send(event_from_hook(raw, args.prompts), args.url)
    except BaseException:  # noqa: BLE001 - including SystemExit from argparse: always exit 0
        pass
    return 0

files.doc: Subscribed projects: a small JSON list in ~/.config/projectviewer/projects.json (local only).

Local viewer server for one or more projects, live.

- GET /api/projects                         -> [{id, name, path, version, last_change}]   (activity)
- GET /api/p/<id>/version                   -> {"version": v}  fingerprint of the Python files (paths, mtimes, sizes)
- GET /api/p/<id>/world                     -> the world (gzip if accepted; ETag = version, 304 when unchanged)
- GET /api/p/<id>/source?file=<path>        -> {"file", "lines"}  only files the analyser itself found
- GET /api/p/<id>/commits                   -> recent commits (subject, notes count, issue refs)
- GET /api/p/<id>/changes?ref=working|<sha> -> changed / affected / notes (see changes.py)
- GET /api/p/<id>/diff?ref=…&file=<path>    -> {"diff"} unified diff of one file in that change set
- GET /api/p/<id>/events?since=<ms>         -> recent AI activity (from the Claude Code hook)
- POST /api/events                          <- `projectviewer hook` (needs header X-ProjectViewer: 1)
- everything else                           -> the built viewer (viewer/dist), single-page-app fallback

Binds to 127.0.0.1 only: nothing is reachable from other machines. The browser polls; the Phase 4
service will push changes instead (Server-Sent Events).
Live AI activity: the Claude Code hook -> server -> viewer feed.

"""Live AI activity: the Claude Code hook -> server -> viewer feed."""

import io
import json
import threading
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

import pytest

from projectviewer.hook import event_from_hook, send
from projectviewer.server import make_server


def post(url, payload, header=True):
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=json.dumps(payload).encode(), method="POST")
    req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    if header:
        req.add_header("X-ProjectViewer", "1")
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=5) as r:
        return r.status


@pytest.fixture
def served(tmp_path):
    root = tmp_path / "shop"
    (root / "shop").mkdir(parents=True)
    (root / "shop/cart.py").write_text("def total():\n    return 1\n")
    srv = make_server([root], port=0, web_dir=tmp_path)
    threading.Thread(target=srv.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
    yield f"http://127.0.0.1:{srv.server_address[1]}", root
    srv.shutdown()
    srv.server_close()


def test_hook_event_for_an_edit():
    ev = event_from_hook(
        {
            "hook_event_name": "PostToolUse",
            "session_id": "s1",
            "cwd": "/w/shop",
            "tool_name": "Edit",
            "tool_input": {"file_path": "/w/shop/shop/cart.py", "old_string": "x", "new_string": "y"},
        },
        prompts=False,
    )
    assert ev == {
        "event": "PostToolUse",
        "session": "s1",
        "cwd": "/w/shop",
        "tool": "Edit",
        "file": "/w/shop/shop/cart.py",
    }


def test_prompts_are_only_recorded_when_switched_on():
    raw = {
        "hook_event_name": "UserPromptSubmit",
        "session_id": "s1",
        "cwd": "/w",
        "prompt": "fix the tax " * 100,
    }
    assert "prompt" not in event_from_hook(raw, prompts=False)
    ev = event_from_hook(raw, prompts=True)
    assert ev["prompt"].startswith("fix the tax") and len(ev["prompt"]) <= 500


def test_send_never_fails_or_blocks_when_no_viewer_runs():
    t = time.perf_counter()
    send(
        {"event": "PostToolUse"}, url="http://127.0.0.1:9/api/events", timeout=0.3
    )  # nothing listens on port 9
    assert time.perf_counter() - t < 1.0


def test_hook_main_always_exits_zero(monkeypatch):
    from projectviewer import hook

    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stdin", io.StringIO("not json"))
    assert hook.main([]) == 0


def test_events_reach_the_right_project_and_are_listed(served):
    base, root = served
    post(
        base + "/api/events",
        {
            "event": "PostToolUse",
            "session": "s1",
            "cwd": str(root),
            "tool": "Edit",
            "file": str(root / "shop/cart.py"),
        },
    )
    post(
        base + "/api/events",
        {
            "event": "PostToolUse",
            "session": "s1",
            "cwd": "/elsewhere",
            "tool": "Edit",
            "file": "/elsewhere/x.py",
        },
    )
    events = json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(base + "/api/p/shop/events").read())
    assert [e["file"] for e in events] == ["shop/cart.py"]  # repo-relative; the unrelated event was dropped
    assert events[0]["tool"] == "Edit" and events[0]["at"] > 0
    projects = json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(base + "/api/projects").read())
    assert projects[0]["last_activity"] == events[0]["at"]


def test_events_without_the_header_are_refused(served):
    base, root = served
    with pytest.raises(urllib.error.HTTPError) as e:
        post(base + "/api/events", {"event": "PostToolUse", "cwd": str(root)}, header=False)
    assert e.value.code == 403


def test_oversized_events_are_refused(served):
    base, root = served
    with pytest.raises(urllib.error.HTTPError) as e:
        post(base + "/api/events", {"event": "x", "cwd": str(root), "pad": "a" * 100_000})
    assert e.value.code == 413

"""What changed, where, why, and what it affects: commits, the live working copy, change notes."""

import subprocess
import textwrap

import pytest

from projectviewer.changes import change_set, commit_list, parse_notes


def git(root, *args):
    return subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", str(root), "-c", "user.name=T", "-c", "user.email=t@example.com", *args],
        check=True,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    ).stdout.strip()


def write(root, rel, code):
    p = root / rel
    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    p.write_text(textwrap.dedent(code).lstrip("\n"))


@pytest.fixture
def repo(tmp_path):
    root = tmp_path / "shop"
    root.mkdir()
    git(root, "init", "-q", "-b", "main")
    write(root, "shop/__init__.py", "")
    write(
        root,
        "shop/cart.py",
        """
        from shop.tax import rate

        def total(x):
            return x * rate()
        """,
    )
    write(root, "shop/tax.py", "def rate():\n    return 1\n")
    write(root, "shop/api.py", "from shop.cart import total\n\ndef checkout():\n    return total(2)\n")
    git(root, "add", "-A")
    git(root, "commit", "-q", "-m", "feat: first version")
    write(root, "shop/tax.py", "def rate():\n    return 2  # new VAT\n\ndef label():\n    return 'vat'\n")
    git(root, "add", "-A")
    git(
        root,
        "commit",
        "-q",
        "-m",
        "fix(tax): new VAT rate\n\nThe rate changed by law.\n\nChanges:\n"
        "- shop/tax.py::rate: changed. Returns the new rate.\n"
        "- shop/tax.py::label: new. Name shown on receipts.\n"
        "- shop/nowhere.py::ghost: a note that matches nothing\n\nRefs #7",
    )
    return root


def test_commit_changes_and_their_impact(repo):
    sha = git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
    cs = change_set(repo, sha)
    assert cs["changed"]["py:shop.tax.rate"] == "modified"
    assert cs["changed"]["py:shop.tax.label"] == "new"
    assert "py:shop.cart.total" not in cs["changed"]
    # who depends on the change: total calls rate; checkout calls total (2 steps)
    assert cs["upstream"]["py:shop.cart.total"] == 1
    assert cs["upstream"]["py:shop.api.checkout"] == 2
    assert cs["files"] == ["shop/tax.py"]
    assert cs["subject"] == "fix(tax): new VAT rate"
    assert cs["refs"] == [7]


def test_change_notes_are_attached_to_symbols(repo):
    cs = change_set(repo, git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD"))
    notes = {n["node"]: n["text"] for n in cs["notes"]}
    assert notes["py:shop.tax.rate"] == "changed. Returns the new rate."
    assert notes["py:shop.tax.label"] == "new. Name shown on receipts."
    assert None in notes  # the note for a symbol that does not exist is kept, unattached


def test_live_working_copy_changes(repo):
    write(repo, "shop/cart.py", "from shop.tax import rate\n\ndef total(x):\n    return x * rate() + 1\n")
    write(repo, "shop/new.py", "def fresh():\n    pass\n")  # untracked file
    cs = change_set(repo, "working")
    assert cs["changed"]["py:shop.cart.total"] == "modified"
    assert cs["changed"]["py:shop.new.fresh"] == "new"
    assert cs["upstream"]["py:shop.api.checkout"] == 1
    assert sorted(cs["files"]) == ["shop/cart.py", "shop/new.py"]


def test_first_commit_has_everything_new(repo):
    first = git(repo, "rev-list", "--max-parents=0", "HEAD")
    cs = change_set(repo, first)
    assert cs["changed"]["py:shop.cart.total"] == "new"


def test_commit_list(repo):
    commits = commit_list(repo)
    assert [c["subject"] for c in commits] == ["fix(tax): new VAT rate", "feat: first version"]
    assert commits[0]["notes"] == 3 and commits[1]["notes"] == 0
    assert commits[0]["refs"] == [7]


def test_parse_notes_formats():
    msg = (
        "subject\n\nbody\n\nChanges:\n"
        "- src/a.py::Cart.total: changed. Line one\n"
        "  continues here.\n"
        "- src/b.py: moved from old/b.py\n"
        "\nnot a note\n"
    )
    notes = parse_notes(msg)
    assert notes == [
        {"path": "src/a.py", "symbol": "Cart.total", "text": "changed. Line one continues here."},
        {"path": "src/b.py", "symbol": None, "text": "moved from old/b.py"},
    ]


def test_moved_files_are_moved_not_removed_and_new(repo):
    (repo / "shop/pricing").mkdir()
    subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", str(repo), "mv", "shop/tax.py", "shop/pricing/tax.py"], check=True, capture_output=True
    )
    (repo / "shop/pricing/__init__.py").write_text("")
    write(repo, "shop/cart.py", "from shop.pricing.tax import rate\n\ndef total(x):\n    return x * rate()\n")
    git(repo, "add", "-A")
    git(repo, "commit", "-q", "-m", "refactor: move tax into pricing")
    cs = change_set(repo, git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD"))
    assert cs["changed"]["py:shop.pricing.tax.rate"] == "moved"
    assert cs["moved"]["py:shop.pricing.tax.rate"] == "py:shop.tax.rate"
    assert "py:shop.tax.rate" not in cs["removed"]
    assert cs["changed"]["file:shop/cart.py"] in ("modified", "contains")
    # a move alone changes no behaviour: it is not a source of impact
    assert "py:shop.api.checkout" not in cs["upstream"]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- review findings (code review, 2026-11-21)


def _move_tax(repo, edit=""):
    (repo / "shop/pricing").mkdir()
    subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", str(repo), "mv", "shop/tax.py", "shop/pricing/tax.py"], check=True, capture_output=True
    )
    (repo / "shop/pricing/__init__.py").write_text("")
    if edit:
        p = repo / "shop/pricing/tax.py"
        p.write_text(p.read_text() + edit)
    git(repo, "add", "-A")
    git(repo, "commit", "-q", "-m", "refactor: move tax")
    return git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD")


def test_diff_of_a_moved_file_shows_only_the_real_edits(repo):
    from projectviewer.changes import file_diff

    sha = _move_tax(repo, edit="\n# moved and edited\n")
    patch = file_diff(repo, sha, "shop/pricing/tax.py")
    assert "new file mode" not in patch
    assert "+# moved and edited" in patch
    assert "+def rate():" not in patch


def test_pure_move_is_listed_in_the_change_files(repo):
    sha = _move_tax(repo)
    assert "shop/pricing/tax.py" in change_set(repo, sha)["files"]


def test_edited_class_in_a_moved_file_still_seeds_impact(repo):
    write(repo, "shop/rates.py", "class Rate:\n    vat = 1\n\n    def get(self):\n        return self.vat\n")
    write(repo, "shop/use.py", "from shop.rates import Rate\n\ndef make():\n    return Rate()\n")
    git(repo, "add", "-A")
    git(repo, "commit", "-q", "-m", "feat: rates")
    (repo / "shop/pricing").mkdir()
    subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", str(repo), "mv", "shop/rates.py", "shop/pricing/rates.py"],
        check=True,
        capture_output=True,
    )
    (repo / "shop/pricing/__init__.py").write_text("")
    write(
        repo,
        "shop/pricing/rates.py",
        "class Rate:\n    vat = 2\n\n    def get(self):\n        return self.vat\n",
    )
    write(repo, "shop/use.py", "from shop.pricing.rates import Rate\n\ndef make():\n    return Rate()\n")
    git(repo, "add", "-A")
    git(repo, "commit", "-q", "-m", "refactor: move rates, change vat")
    cs = change_set(repo, git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD"))
    assert cs["changed"]["py:shop.pricing.rates.Rate"] == "modified"
    assert cs["changed"]["py:shop.pricing.rates.Rate.get"] == "moved"
    assert "py:shop.use.make" in cs["upstream"]


def test_working_copy_detects_a_plain_mv_without_git(repo):
    (repo / "shop/pricing").mkdir()
    (repo / "shop/tax.py").rename(repo / "shop/pricing/tax.py")
    cs = change_set(repo, "working")
    assert cs["changed"]["py:shop.pricing.tax.rate"] == "moved"
    assert "py:shop.tax.rate" not in cs["removed"]


def test_untracked_file_with_a_space_in_its_name(repo):
    write(repo, "shop/my tool.py", "def run():\n    pass\n")
    cs = change_set(repo, "working")
    assert cs["changed"]["file:shop/my tool.py"] == "new"


def test_head_change_set_follows_new_commits(repo):
    from projectviewer.server import Project

    p = Project("shop", repo, None)
    first = p.changes("HEAD")["sha"]
    write(repo, "shop/more.py", "def more():\n    pass\n")
    git(repo, "add", "-A")
    git(repo, "commit", "-q", "-m", "feat: more")
    assert p.changes("HEAD")["sha"] != first


def test_notes_from_several_changes_sections_as_in_a_squash_commit():
    msg = (
        "feat: big PR (#4)\n\n* feat: first\n\nChanges:\n- a.py::f: new. First.\n\n"
        "* fix: second\n\nChanges:\n- b.py::g: changed. Second.\n"
    )
    assert [n["symbol"] for n in parse_notes(msg)] == ["f", "g"]

files.doc: Specification of the Python cartographer (ADR-0002 world format).
The local viewer server: several projects, world API, live version, source, changes, static files.
files.source:
"""The local viewer server: several projects, world API, live version, source, changes, static files."""

import gzip
import json
import subprocess
import threading
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request

import pytest

from projectviewer.server import make_server


def get(url, headers=None):
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers=headers or {})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=20) as r:
        return r.status, dict(r.headers), r.read()


def getj(url):
    return json.loads(get(url)[2])


def start(roots, web):
    srv = make_server(roots, port=0, web_dir=web)
    threading.Thread(target=srv.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
    return srv, f"http://127.0.0.1:{srv.server_address[1]}"


@pytest.fixture
def two_projects(tmp_path):
    shop = tmp_path / "shop"
    (shop / "shop").mkdir(parents=True)
    (shop / "shop/__init__.py").write_text("")
    (shop / "shop/orders.py").write_text("def total():\n    return 1\n")
    lib = tmp_path / "library"
    (lib / "books").mkdir(parents=True)
    (lib / "books/loans.py").write_text("def lend():\n    pass\n")
    web = tmp_path / "web"
    web.mkdir()
    (web / "index.html").write_text("<html>viewer</html>")
    srv, base = start([shop, lib], web)
    yield base, shop, lib
    srv.shutdown()
    srv.server_close()


def test_projects_are_listed_with_ids_and_activity(two_projects):
    base, shop, lib = two_projects
    projects = getj(base + "/api/projects")
    assert [p["id"] for p in projects] == ["shop", "library"]
    assert projects[0]["path"] == str(shop.resolve())
    assert all(p["last_change"] > 0 and p["version"] for p in projects)


def test_each_project_has_its_own_world(two_projects):
    base, _, _ = two_projects
    shop = getj(base + "/api/p/shop/world")
    lib = getj(base + "/api/p/library/world")
    assert "py:shop.orders.total" in {n["id"] for n in shop["nodes"]}
    assert "py:books.loans.lend" in {n["id"] for n in lib["nodes"]}


def test_unknown_project_is_404(two_projects):
    base, _, _ = two_projects
    with pytest.raises(urllib.error.HTTPError) as e:
        get(base + "/api/p/nope/world")
    assert e.value.code == 404


def test_world_is_gzipped_and_cached_with_etag(two_projects):
    base, _, _ = two_projects
    _, headers, body = get(base + "/api/p/shop/world", {"Accept-Encoding": "gzip"})
    assert headers.get("Content-Encoding") == "gzip"
    assert json.loads(gzip.decompress(body))["schema"] == "project-world/1"
    with pytest.raises(urllib.error.HTTPError) as e:
        get(base + "/api/p/shop/world", {"If-None-Match": headers["ETag"]})
    assert e.value.code == 304


def test_activity_follows_the_project_that_changed(two_projects):
    base, shop, _ = two_projects
    before = {p["id"]: p for p in getj(base + "/api/projects")}
    time.sleep(0.02)
    (shop / "shop/orders.py").write_text("def total():\n    return 2\n\ndef tax():\n    return 0\n")
    after = {p["id"]: p for p in getj(base + "/api/projects")}
    assert after["shop"]["version"] != before["shop"]["version"]
    assert after["shop"]["last_change"] > before["shop"]["last_change"]
    assert after["library"]["version"] == before["library"]["version"]
    world = getj(base + "/api/p/shop/world")
    assert world["version"] == after["shop"]["version"]
    assert "py:shop.orders.tax" in {n["id"] for n in world["nodes"]}


def test_source_returns_lines_of_a_project_file(two_projects):
    base, _, _ = two_projects
    assert getj(base + "/api/p/shop/source?file=shop/orders.py")["lines"][0] == "def total():"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "bad", ["../etc/passwd", "/etc/passwd", "shop/../../secret.py", "nope.py", "books/loans.py"]
)
def test_source_refuses_anything_outside_the_projects_files(two_projects, bad):
    base, _, _ = two_projects
    with pytest.raises(urllib.error.HTTPError) as e:
        get(base + "/api/p/shop/source?file=" + urllib.parse.quote(bad))
    assert e.value.code == 404


def test_changes_commits_and_diff(two_projects):
    base, shop, _ = two_projects

    def git(*a):
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", str(shop), "-c", "user.name=T", "-c", "user.email=t@example.com", *a],
            check=True,
            capture_output=True,
        )

    git("init", "-q", "-b", "main")
    git("add", "-A")
    git("commit", "-q", "-m", "feat: orders\n\nChanges:\n- shop/orders.py::total: new. Order total.")
    commits = getj(base + "/api/p/shop/commits")
    assert commits[0]["subject"] == "feat: orders" and commits[0]["notes"] == 1
    cs = getj(base + f"/api/p/shop/changes?ref={commits[0]['sha']}")
    assert cs["changed"]["py:shop.orders.total"] == "new"
    assert cs["notes"][0]["node"] == "py:shop.orders.total"
    (shop / "shop/orders.py").write_text("def total():\n    return 3\n")
    live = getj(base + "/api/p/shop/changes?ref=working")
    assert live["changed"]["py:shop.orders.total"] == "modified"
    patch = getj(base + "/api/p/shop/diff?ref=working&file=shop/orders.py")["diff"]
    assert "-    return 1" in patch and "+    return 3" in patch


@pytest.mark.parametrize("ref", ["--output=/tmp/x", "HEAD;rm", "../x", ""])
def test_changes_refuse_odd_refs(two_projects, ref):
    base, _, _ = two_projects
    with pytest.raises(urllib.error.HTTPError) as e:
        get(base + "/api/p/shop/changes?ref=" + urllib.parse.quote(ref))
    assert e.value.code == 400


def test_static_files_and_spa_fallback(two_projects):
    base, _, _ = two_projects
    assert get(base + "/")[2] == b"<html>viewer</html>"
    assert get(base + "/some/client/route")[2] == b"<html>viewer</html>"


def test_missing_viewer_build_shows_instructions(tmp_path):
    (tmp_path / "a.py").write_text("")
    srv, base = start([tmp_path], tmp_path / "does-not-exist")
    try:
        assert "npm run build" in get(base + "/")[2].decode()
    finally:
        srv.shutdown()
        srv.server_close()


def test_binds_to_localhost_only(tmp_path):
    srv = make_server([tmp_path], port=0, web_dir=tmp_path)
    try:
        assert srv.server_address[0] == "127.0.0.1"
    finally:
        srv.server_close()


def test_registry_add_list_remove(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    from projectviewer import registry

    monkeypatch.setenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", str(tmp_path / "cfg"))
    (tmp_path / "a").mkdir()
    (tmp_path / "b").mkdir()
    assert registry.add(tmp_path / "a")["id"] == "a"
    assert registry.add(tmp_path / "a")["id"] == "a"  # adding twice is harmless
    registry.add(tmp_path / "b")
    assert [p["id"] for p in registry.load()] == ["a", "b"]
    assert registry.remove("a") is True
    assert [p["id"] for p in registry.load()] == ["b"]

files.doc: One place for every colour on the map (RGB arrays for deck.gl).

Layout of ONE level of the folder tree: the children of the current focus become blocks on a
ground plane, separated by "streets". Size = number of functions inside (lines of code when every
block on the level is a single function). Footprint grows gently with size, so small things stay
clickable; height grows with size relative to the biggest sibling (bigger = clearly taller).

The world as an index: lookups, test reach, links for a selection, group-level overview links.
Pure functions (no React, no DOM), unit-tested with `npm test`.
Unit tests for the viewer's pure logic. Run: npm test  (Node's built-in test runner)

The project as a FOLDER tree: root › folders › files › classes › functions (+ a Database block for
tables). The map shows one level of it at a time. Pure logic, unit-tested with `npm test`.

Cameras: 2D flat map and the 2.5D city (tilted orthographic orbit view, as in PR World v5).
The app keeps the camera in LAYOUT coordinates (y grows downwards). deck.gl's orbit view has y
pointing up, so y is negated when talking to it.

symbols.name: module_name
symbols.doc: 'src/shop/orders.py' -> 'src.shop.orders'; '__init__.py' names the package.

symbols.name: sql_tables
symbols.doc: [(table, 'reads'|'writes')] found in one SQL string.

symbols.name: chain_of
symbols.doc: Callee expression as tokens, or None when it isn't a simple name/attribute/call chain.

symbols.name: _strings
symbols.doc: String constants and f-strings inside statements (f-string holes become a space).

symbols.name: _body_facts
symbols.doc:
Calls, local variable types, SQL tables, HTTP requests and nested definitions found in a list
of statements. Nested function/class bodies are included: their effects belong to the enclosing code.

symbols.name: _http_request
symbols.doc: `client.get("/orders/42?x=1")` -> {"verb": "GET", "path": "/orders/42"}: a test talking to an API.

symbols.name: _result_spec
symbols.doc:
Type spec of the first value returned or yielded: used when there is no return annotation,
e.g. pytest fixtures (`eng = Engine(); yield eng`).

symbols.name: discover
symbols.doc:
Python files, as repo-relative posix paths. Uses git (respects .gitignore, includes new
untracked files) when available, otherwise walks the directory.

symbols.name: git_files
symbols.doc:
(path, content) of the Python files in a commit, read from git objects: the working tree is
never touched. One `git cat-file --batch` process for all files.

symbols.name: _analyse
symbols.doc: Pass 1 for (path, bytes) items: from the cache when possible, parsed (maybe in parallel) otherwise.

symbols.name: map_repo
symbols.doc:
The working tree (including uncommitted and untracked files). workers: processes for parsing
cache misses. None = automatic (parallel only when there are enough misses); 1 = always serial.

symbols.name: map_revision
symbols.doc: A commit, read from git objects (the working tree is not touched).

symbols.name: group_of
symbols.doc: Top-level grouping shown as a district on the map.

symbols.name: Ctx
symbols.doc: Where a name is being resolved.

symbols.name: _instance
symbols.doc: type_of() result -> resolution result.

symbols.name: resolve_dotted
symbols.doc: 'pkg.mod.Class.method' -> result, following re-exports.

symbols.name: mro
symbols.doc: The class and its project-defined base classes, breadth first.

symbols.name: fixture_type
symbols.doc: Type of a pytest fixture parameter: same module first, then the nearest conftest.py.

symbols.name: scope
symbols.doc: Resolve the first token of a chain, following Python's lookup order.

symbols.name: lookup_expr
symbols.doc: Resolve a written name like 'Base' or 'pkg.Base' (no calls).

symbols.name: resolve_chain
symbols.doc: A callee chain such as ['cart', 'total'] -> result.

symbols.name: call_result
symbols.doc: What calling `thing` returns.

symbols.name: type_of
symbols.doc: Project class (qualified name), EXTERNAL, BUILTIN, or None.

symbols.name: _annotation_names
symbols.doc: Dotted names inside an annotation string, e.g. 'requests.Session | None' -> ['requests.Session', 'None'].

symbols.name: parse_notes
symbols.doc:
The bullet lists under every line `Changes:` (each until a blank line or a non-bullet,
non-indented line). Several sections occur when commits are squashed into one.

symbols.name: note_target
symbols.doc: Node id a note talks about: a symbol (py:module.Qual.name) or a whole file.

symbols.name: changed_lines
symbols.doc:
`git diff -U0` -> {file: [(first, last)]} on the new side. Pure deletions mark the line where
they happened.

symbols.name: renames
symbols.doc: {new path: old path} for files git sees as moved (rename detection, -M).

symbols.name: _old_id
symbols.doc: The id the same thing had before its file was moved (ids are derived from paths).

symbols.name: plain_moves
symbols.doc:
{new path: old path} for files moved WITHOUT git (plain `mv`, an editor rename): a tracked file
that disappeared and an untracked file with similar content. git cannot see these yet.

symbols.name: working_moves
symbols.doc: All moves in the working copy: git-tracked (`git mv`, staged) and plain ones.

symbols.name: change_set
symbols.doc: ref = "working" (uncommitted changes vs HEAD, including untracked files) or a commit.

symbols.name: commit_list
symbols.doc: Recent commits, newest first, with how many change notes and issue references each has.

symbols.name: file_diff
symbols.doc:
Unified diff of one file for a change set (the "how"). For a moved file it compares with the
old path, so it shows only the real edits, not the whole file as new.

symbols.name: Project
symbols.doc: One repository: its current world (rebuilt only when files change) and its change sets.

symbols.name: fingerprint
symbols.doc: (version, last change in ms): cheap, from paths + mtimes + sizes of the Python files.

symbols.name: current
symbols.doc: (version, json bytes, gzipped json bytes); re-maps only if the version changed.

symbols.name: project
symbols.doc: Write a small fixture project: project({"pkg/a.py": "code", ...}) -> root path.

symbols.name: W
symbols.doc: Small query helper over a world dict, to keep assertions readable.

symbols.name: roofTiles
symbols.doc:
The roof of a block, divided into its children (one level deep): shows how a module is organised
without opening it. Area follows the same size measure as the blocks. No division for 0–1 children.

symbols.name: curve
symbols.doc: Curved link between two points (quadratic Bézier), as a polyline for deck.gl's PathLayer.

symbols.name: curve3d
symbols.doc: Arc between two block tops, lifted in the middle in proportion to its length.

symbols.name: fit
symbols.doc: Camera that fits a rectangle into a viewport of (width x height) pixels (flat map).

symbols.name: linksFor
symbols.doc: Links between the selected thing (including everything inside it) and the rest of the world.

symbols.name: groupLinks
symbols.doc: Overview: how the top-level groups depend on each other (calls, instantiation, data access).

symbols.name: displayName
symbols.doc: Short human name: methods get their class, scripts their file.

symbols.name: blockIndex
symbols.doc: Map every world node inside `focus` to the child block of `focus` that contains it.

symbols.name: levelLinks
symbols.doc: Dependencies between the blocks of one level, summed: calls, object creation, and data access.

symbols.name: blockDeps
symbols.doc:
Links from a block to everything outside it, summed per sibling block at the current level. When the
other end lies outside the current level, it is named by its top-level module, marked "@" (elsewhere).

symbols.name: changeMarks
symbols.doc:
Change overlay: a block is "changed" when anything inside it changed, else "affected" when anything
inside it depends on or is reached by the change.

symbols.name: fitView
symbols.doc: Camera that frames box r (with its towers, up to r.zTop) in the current view mode.
